messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: High GPU memory churn observed in kv-cache on prod-gpu-2. Multiple nodes showing rapid growth in KV arena allocations; customer-facing latency spikes reported. Paging oncall.
sam: on it — ack. grabbing logs, standing by. which customers affected?
maya: saw alerts from latency-detector for /v1/generate on cluster west-1. Errors 500 and timeouts ~10-20% of requests for a subset of requests. Customers: acme-corp and a few PLG sandbox orgs. :eyes:
sam: here's tail from node prod-gpu-2 (truncated):
```
2026-03-15T02:12:03Z kv_cache.cpp:842 allocate_arena: arena growth from 1.2G -> 3.9G in 4s
2026-03-15T02:12:04Z runtime: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
2026-03-15T02:12:05Z batcher.cpp:477 continuous_batch_loop: inflight shards=128 batch_size=64
2026-03-15T02:12:06Z kv_cache.cpp:900 compaction skipped: active_kv_chains > threshold
```
sam: looks like continuous-batching + kv cache fragmentation causing allocator thrash -> cudaMalloc fails -> fallbacks -> latency.
niko: adding context: we recently rolled batcher v2 that increases warmup parallelism. Could be that the new config exposes a fragmentation cliff for long-running KV caches.
devon: @sam can you check whether compaction daemon is stuck? maybe compaction paused due to high load.
sam: compaction process is running but reports low reclaimed bytes. I can run a manual compaction on the node.
ash: tagging ops-bot to capture metrics snapshot: @ops-bot snapshot node=prod-gpu-2 interval=5m
ops-bot: Metrics snapshot created: https://internal.metrics/redwood/prod-gpu-2/snapshot/2064009876
maya: quick mitigation idea: reduce continuous_batch_size for the route to avoid large ephemeral KV writes that bloat the arena. Also drop batcher parallelism to limit concurrent allocations.
sam: agree. preparing a soft rollback of batcher config to previous values for west-1. will patch feature flag.
niko: also consider forcing a compaction pass after reducing throughput. compaction + smaller batches should let arena reclaim.
devon: note: compaction can be CPU-heavy; do it staged. we should do one node first then drive others.
sam: executing config change on canary subset (prod-gpu-2a, prod-gpu-2b). command:
```
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/batcher CONTINUOUS_BATCH_SIZE=8 CONT_BATCH_PARALLELISM=4
kubectl rollout restart deploy/batcher -n inference
```
sam: rolled on canary. watching logs.
maya: logs show batch_size reduced and continuous_batch_loop entries down from 64->8. GPU mem growth slowed on 2a.
ops-bot: Alert: latency spike subsided on canary nodes within 35s of rollout. Confirmed by synthetic checks.
niko: good. schedule compaction run on the canary nodes now. command:
```
ssh prod-gpu-2a 'sudo /usr/local/bin/kv_compactor --run-once --aggressive'
```
devon: compaction reclaimed ~1.6G on 2a. memory usage dropped to expected baseline.
sam: starting staged rollout to remaining west-1 nodes with same env change and restart. doing 3 at a time.
ash: raising customer comms: engineering lead contact for acme-corp notified. drafting note: "We're investigating elevated latency; mitigation underway; will follow up with RCA." @maya please review.
maya: LGTM. include temporary config tweak and that we're monitoring.
ops-bot: Rolling update progress: 2/8 nodes done, next batch queued.

--- 45 minutes later ---
ops-bot: All west-1 nodes rolled. Global metrics show request latency back within SLOs. No further OOMs observed.
sam: opening follow-up actions: 1) revert batcher-v2 aggressive defaults 2) add allocator telemetry for kv arena fragmentation (per-chain fragmentation metric) 3) schedule postmortem + assign owner.
niko: + add a canary test for long-running KV-heavy traffic pattern to detect fragmentation cliff.
devon: create a runbook entry for manual compaction + safe thresholds. include compaction throttles and CPU impact notes.
ash: I'll own the customer follow-up and send a post-incident update to acme-corp and affected orgs.
sam: postmortem owner? @niko can you take lead on RCA and remediation plan?
niko: I can. I'll trig RCA doc and invite eng-runtime, eng-ml, and devex. initial hypothesis: batcher-v2 increased parallel allocation patterns causing interleaved free/alloc sequences that fragment the arena, leading to repeated cudaMalloc/pyTorch fallback and eventual OOMs. corollary: compaction heuristics need to be more aggressive or triggered earlier under this workload.
maya: quick items in RCA doc: include timings of compaction runs, sequence of allocation sizes, kernel selection logs, and quantization/alloc path differences. also surface customer-requested SLAs.
sam: additional mitigation: add guardrail in batcher to limit inflight shards for routes with high kv retention. will open PR to enforce per-route max_inflight_shards.
ops-bot: Incident resolved: mitigation deployed and validated. Recording incident severity: Sev2. Reference snapshots: https://internal.metrics/.../2064009876

--- final notes ---
devon: timeline: 02:12 pager -> 02:55 full west-1 mitigation in place -> 03:40 all clear and monitoring stable.
niko: planned follow-ups: allocator telemetry, compaction tuning, batcher canary tests, PR for inflight guards. target ETA for fixes: 2 weeks.
ash: I'll send customer update in 1h and postmortem once RCA doc is ready.
sam: thanks all. great faster triage and staged rollout. :thumbsup:
